name: GA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean makes this deeply Republican territory
Clyde's overwhelming fundraising edge: $671k raised versus $43k for Gegen
Prediction markets price Clyde's win probability around 95%
No public polls or expert ratings; race has drawn little outside attention
model.rationale: The seat's seventeen-point Republican lean, Clyde's incumbency and dominant financial position, and market pricing near 95 percent for the GOP all point the same way. With no polling suggesting vulnerability and only token outside spending against the incumbent, an upset is highly unlikely.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Clyde or a sharply improved Democratic national environment could narrow the margin, though it would likely still fall well short of an upset.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 9th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly seventeen points toward the GOP. Andrew Clyde has held the seat since 2021 and enters the general election as a heavy favorite after being renominated. Caitlyn Gegen, the Democratic nominee, has raised only about $43,000 and had under $5,000 on hand, leaving her little capacity to introduce herself to voters.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put Clyde's chances around 95 percent. His fundraising advantage, the district's entrenched lean, and an environment that has favored Republicans this cycle all point in the same direction. An upset would require a dramatic shift; the realistic question is the size of Clyde's winning margin, likely in the mid-to-high teens.
